3294-the-sea-hawk:
Raphael Sabatini builds this adventure around Sir Oliver Tressilian of Cornwall. Part one follows the huckster, Rosamund, the forge, and the intervener, through the buckler, Jasper Leigh, and a trepanning, to the Spaniard who seals his fate. Betrayed and sold into slavery, Oliver vanishes from England and returns under another name.

Part two names him Sakr-el-Bahr, the hawk of the sea. The captive, the renegade, and the homeward bound lead to the raid, the lion of the faith, and the convert. Marzak-ben-Asad waits among his foes. Sabatini writes swashbuckling romance at its best: a gentleman turned corsair, seeking justice on the sea that wronged him.
podcast-joerogan-ZIcQwDkcaWk:
Researcher Lex Fridman visits Joe Rogan for episode 1422, an early meeting of the two hosts. Fridman would later become a major podcaster himself. He arrives in his trademark black suit and tie.

Rogan teases him about dressing so sharply for a casual show. Fridman calls the suit armor that helps him focus. From there the talk opens into science, machines, and big ideas. The episode is a good record of Fridman before fame, when his calm style and deep curiosity were already fully formed. That ease marks all of his later visits too.
podcast-tuckercarlson-eat9NlWfKwk:
Romanian politician Calin Georgescu tells Tucker Carlson that Antony Blinken and Emmanuel Macron killed Romanian democracy. Georgescu won the first round of Romania's presidential vote before courts annulled the result and barred him. He presents himself as a banned opposition leader robbed of an election.

Georgescu lays out his charge that Western officials pushed Romania to cancel the people's choice. He describes the legal moves used against his campaign. Carlson asks what the case means for democracy across Europe. Concerned and freedom-minded viewers get a stolen-vote claim from the man at its center.
